https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/09/06/neme.text: Menü Kereső Orbán Viktor gratulált az AfD „földcsuszamlásszerű győzelméhez” Külföld Tenczer Gábor Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom „Hatalmas este ez Németországnak és Európának” – írta Orbán Viktor az X-en a német Szász-Anhalt tartományi választások első eredményeire reagálva. Hozzátette: „Gratulálok Alice Weidelnek, Ulrich Siegmundnak és az egész AfD-nek a földcsuszamlásszerű győzelemhez Szász-Anhaltban. Kapaszkodjatok meg! Ez még csak a kezdet!” Nem csoda, hogy sietett gratulálni, Orbán már 2025-ben olyan nyilatkozatot tett , hogy az AfD a jövő. Orbánhoz csatlakozott Matteo Salvini olasz miniszterelnök-helyettes is, elsöprő sikernek nevezve a győzelmet, annak ellenére, hogy „a baloldal folyamatosan félelmeket szít és katasztrofális forgatókönyveket gyárt”. Mint beszámoltunk róla, a szélsőjobboldali Alternatíva Németországért (AfD) párt 44 százalék körüli szavazatot kapott az exit pollok szerint a kelet-németországi Szász-Anhalt tartományban a vasárnapi választáson. A CDU 18 százalék, a Linke 9 százalék, a szociáldemokraták 9 százalék körül lehetnek. A Zöldek javítva korábbi eredményükön szintén 9 százalékon állhatnak, az újonnan alapított Sahra Wagenknecht Szövetség (BSW) pedig az 5 százalékos küszöb körül billeg. Az FDP várhatóan nem jut be a tartományi parlamentbe. A nagy kérdés még nem dőlt el, hogy az AfD képes lesz-e egyedül abszolút többséget szerezni és ezzel kormányra jutni Szász-Anhalt tartományban. A 2,1 millió lakost számláló Szász-Anhaltban a választás alapesetben csak a német belpolitika követőit és a szász-anhaltiakat érdekelte volna, azonban most az egész világ figyelt. Ez az első választás, ahol már nem az a kérdés, hogy a szélsőjobboldali Alternatíva Németországértnak (AfD) lesz-e a legtöbb képviselője a tartományi parlamentben, hanem az, hogy összejön-e az abszolút többség, vagy a többi párt összefogásával megakadályozható, hogy megválasszák az AfD első tartományi miniszterelnökét, írtuk . The poll also revealed differing views on Polish leadership, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk viewed positively by 45% of respondents, while President Karol Nawrocki received a 62% negative rating. Meanwhile, France, the UK, and Germany topped the list of nations perceived as friendly by Ukrainians. by TVP World | Aug. 30, 2026, 9:28 am Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied People hold a giant Ukraine-Poland joint national flag during a demonstration as part of a mock referendum about a mock annexation of the Russian Embassy to Poland, in front of the Russian Embassy in Warsaw, Poland, Oct. 15, 2022. (Photo by Wojtek RADWANSKI / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip Only half of Ukrainians now consider Poland a friendly country, a sharp decline from previous years, according to a new Rating Group survey. The poll found that 50% of respondents saw Poland’s attitude toward Ukraine as friendly, while 21% considered it hostile. In February 2024, 79% described Poland as friendly, down from 94% in 2023. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . A separate poll conducted in March 2024 also showed worsening perceptions. At the time, 58% of Ukrainians said they had a positive attitude toward Poland . That survey asked a different question and is therefore not directly comparable with the Rating Group figures. Poland drops behind other allies In the latest poll, France was considered friendly by 81% of respondents, followed by the UK at 80%, and Germany and Lithuania at 77%. Moldova was rated friendly by 68%, Romania by 56% and the US by 54%. Advertisement Views of Polish politicians also differed sharply. Prime Minister Donald Tusk was viewed positively by 45% of Ukrainians and negatively by 35%, while President Karol Nawrocki received 20% positive and 62% negative ratings. By comparison, Nawrocki’s predecessor, Andrzej Duda, was viewed positively by 72% of respondents in February 2025. Rating Group surveyed a representative sample of 2,000 Ukrainian adults between August 4 and 9. The poll excluded Russian-occupied territories and areas without Ukrainian mobile coverage. https://www.politico.eu/article/germany-.text: Germany's chief of defense Carsten Breuer will take over as chair of NATO's highest military authority, after a majority of the alliance's top generals backed his candidacy in a secret vote on Saturday. Breuer, who has led Germany's armed forces since 2023, won the support of at least 17 of NATO's 32 chiefs of defense during a closed-door ballot to become the chair of NATO's military committee in Copenhagen. "Congratulations to General Carsten Breuer," the current chair, Italy's Adm. Giuseppe Cavo Dragone wrote on X , announcing the decision. "Your operational judgement, your deep familiarity with this Alliance and your leadership of the German Armed Forces will serve NATO well." Advertisement Advertisement Breuer will take over from Dragone next July and will serve a three-year term. The rest of the votes were kept secret to avoid the risk of breeding disloyalty and divisions over the result, said one NATO official, who was granted anonymity to speak freely. The German four-star general beat Canada's chief of defense Jennie Carignan for the role. He was seen as the favorite given Berlin's status as Europe’s top defense spender and implicit backing from Washington. Breuer had campaigned on Germany's leading role in defense spending as European allies come under U.S. pressure to take control of their own defense. Carignan, Ottawa’s top general since 2024, made her pitch about reinvigorating the role of the military committee and signaling enduring transatlantic unity inside NATO. Strained bilateral ties between Canada and the U.S. were seen by NATO officials as making Carignan’s case more difficult. The result underscores Berlin's growing role in the alliance, as it takes over senior military roles and assumes greater operational responsibility for protecting frontline states with a regional army command focused on Estonia and Latvia and a permanent deployment in Lithuania. The chair of NATO’s military committee is expected to give honest military advice to allies — helping assess the feasibility, financing and capabilities of operations. They oversee dozens of working groups of NATO military staff, and broker consensus on formulating military advice. Advertisement Advertisement
